chunks: If it is said: On what criterion have you justified these reports and claim that Imam Kadhim (a.s) is dead, whereas the Waqifiya have also narrated a large number of reports, which mention his being alive and that His Eminence is the Qaim is hinted at. These traditional reports are present in their books and even in books of your scholars. So, how can you reconcile these two types of traditional reports? And with attention to these traditional reports, how can you claim that he is dead?

We would reply: We mentioned these traditional reports by way of information and announcement and not to prove his death from them. It is so, because there exists knowledge of his martyrdom (it is a definite matter) and there is no doubt in it. Like the knowledge of martyrdom of his respected ancestors and one who has doubt in the martyrdom of Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s), he can also doubt the martyrdom of his respected ancestors and it is possible to doubt the death of anyone whose information of death we have. We have mentioned these traditional reports only to emphasize the information, because a large number of reports create this knowledge for us through evidence, Shariah, apparent aspect of Quran, consensus and other reasonings. Thus, I mentioned them in this chapter only for emphasis.

As for that, which the Waqifiya have narrated: (Firstly) All of them are solitary reports and no evidence and reasoning strengthens them; and it is impossible to claim that they are authentic. (Secondly) In addition, their narrators have also been targets of ridicule and they were unreliable and it is not possible to trust their statements and reports. (Thirdly) With all these explanations all their reports can be interpreted and justified in other ways.
We will quote some of them from Fee Nusratul Waqifa of Abu Muhammad Ali Ahmad Alawi Musawi and explain his discussions.

key_terms.أَخْبَارُ أَحَادٍ: Solitary reports narrated by a single chain of narrators, which do not yield definitive knowledge.
key_terms.إِجْمَاعٌ: Consensus, specifically among scholars or the community.
key_terms.الاسْتِظْهَارُ: Seeking clarification or emphasis through additional evidence.
key_terms.الوَاقِفَةُ: The Waqifiya, a Shia sect that stopped believing in the succession of Imam Musa al-Kadim (a.s) and claimed he did not die.
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Definitive knowledge or certainty, as opposed to mere opinion or probability.
key_terms.مَطْعُونٌ عَلَيْهِمْ: Having a flaw or defect attributed to them, often referring to reliability in narration.

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile reports of Imam Musa al-Kadim's (a.s) death with the Waqifiya's claim that he is still alive?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi establishes that the Imam's death is a matter of definitive knowledge (al-ilm bi-mawtihi), comparable to the certain death of his forefathers, rather than a matter of probabilistic inference. He dismisses the Waqifiya's evidence as weak solitary reports (akhbar al-ahad) with questionable narrators, arguing that these are merely interpretive possibilities rather than proofs of immortality. This distinction reinforces the Shia epistemological stance that major events in the Imam's life are known with certainty, while minor details may rely on less rigorous transmission.
